name: Marcus T.
text: This is spot-on. I went to a private dinner in Napa last month where they piped in this subtle lavender scent during the aperitif course, and I swear it made me more relaxed and open to conversation. The host was clearly thinking about every sensory detail.

name: Elena R.
text: Question: how do you balance scent so it doesn't overpower the food aromas? I'd imagine that's tricky at a dinner event where smell is half the dining experience.

name: James W.
text: I disagree that scent is 'invisible.' When it's done wrong at these fancy events, that artificial floral smell is all anyone notices. Less is definitely more.

name: Sophie B.
text: The memory connection is real. A friend's wedding reception used a custom scent inspired by the couple's honeymoon destination, and now whenever I smell it, I'm transported back to that night. Genius move for experiential design.

name: David K.
text: Great article but would have loved more specifics on which scents work best for different menu types or time of day. Any recommendations?
